finding.claim: dropTable ignores the error returned by Authorize, so the authorization check is not enforced. Any request that has a user in its context can drop tables without the 'dba' role.
finding.source: Any authenticated (non-dba) user calling POST /admin/drop with form value t

trace.note: /admin/drop routed to dropTable with no middleware
Authorize result discarded; forbidden error never acted on

finding.guards_checked: Authorize is called but its return value is dropped. Compare vacuum at api.go:33-36, which checks it. No other middleware on the mux.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) returns an error, but dropTable discards it at api.go:26; vacuum checks it at api.go:33. The only other incidental barrier is the unchecked type assertion in userFrom (api.go:22), which panics when no user is in the context. Nothing in the repo sets that value, and there is no middleware on the mux (api.go:44-46).
verdict.reason: api.go:26 calls Authorize as a bare statement, so the forbidden error never stops api.go:27 from running DROP TABLE with the user-supplied table name; any request with a non-dba user in its context reaches the drop (an anonymous request panics at api.go:22), and nothing in this repo populates that context value, so exploitability depends on auth middleware outside it.

finding.claim: SQL injection: the table name from the request is concatenated directly into a DROP TABLE statement, with no allowlist or identifier quoting. The caller can inject arbitrary SQL such as 'x; DROP DATABASE ...', or drop any table.

trace.note: r.FormValue("t") concatenated into SQL string and passed to runSQL

finding.guards_checked: No validation, allowlist or quoting. The only guard is Authorize, which is not enforced (see F1). Even with it enforced, a dba could still inject. runSQL is a stub here, so the real driver's multi-statement behaviour is unknown.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 returns an error, but the result is discarded as a bare statement, so it is not enforced. There is no allowlist, quoting or parameterization. No auth middleware exists in the directory (main registers the handler directly at api.go:44).
verdict.reason: api.go:27 concatenates r.FormValue("t") into "DROP TABLE " + ... and passes it to runSQL, and the Authorize result at api.go:26 is ignored, so any caller can reach it; runSQL at api.go:41 is only a stub, so how the real driver handles multi-statement strings is unknown, but dropping an arbitrary table is possible.

finding.claim: userFrom does an unchecked type assertion on the context value. If no auth middleware set "user", the assertion panics. Nothing in this code sets the user at all, so the endpoints have no visible authentication. Impact is limited because net/http recovers the panic per request, but the result is an unauthenticated 500 or a fail-open if auth is expected elsewhere.

trace.note: non-comma-ok type assertion on a nil interface panics

finding.guards_checked: No authentication middleware appears in this file. Only api.go exists, so middleware elsewhere can't be ruled out. The panic is recovered by net/http's per-connection handler, so it is not a process-wide DoS.

verdict.guard_found: none: no auth middleware exists, but the unchecked assertion at api.go:22 panics before any handler effect (runSQL at api.go:27/37), so it fails closed. net/http recovers the panic per request.
verdict.reason: The lines match the trace (api.go:22 unchecked assertion, api.go:44 bare HandleFunc), but main is the only entry point (api.go:43-46) and nothing sets "user", so every request panics at api.go:22 before runSQL at api.go:27 or 37 and no privileged action runs; the "fail-open" claim is false and the real impact is only a per-request aborted connection, not a security vulnerability.
